gaps.sentence: I'm afraid your passport is ___ — it expired last month (VALID).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: it has expired
gaps.explanation: An expired document is invalid (in- + valid); an adjective is needed after 'is'.

gaps.sentence: The magazine ___ the politician's words, which caused a scandal (QUOTE).
gaps.hint: quoted wrongly — that is why there was a scandal (mis-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misquoted explains the scandal. The past tense is needed.

gaps.sentence: There has been a big ___ (IMPROVE) in her tennis.
gaps.explanation: After 'a big' a noun is needed: improvement (-ment noun).

gaps.sentence: The audience found the lecture extremely ___ (BORE).
gaps.explanation: The lecture causes boredom, so it is boring; the audience would be bored.

gaps.sentence: The storm caused serious ___ (DESTROY) along the coast.
gaps.explanation: After the adjective 'serious' a noun is needed: destruction (-tion noun).

gaps.sentence: He ___ forgets to bring the tickets, as usual (TYPICAL).
gaps.hint: adverb of frequency needed to modify 'forgets' (-ly)
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'forgets': typically means in the usual way.

gaps.sentence: He had a happy ___ in the countryside (CHILD).
gaps.hint: noun needed: the period of being a child (-hood)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -hood forms period-of-life nouns: childhood.

gaps.sentence: The report highlighted the ___ of sport in schools (IMPORTANT).
gaps.explanation: After 'the' a noun is needed: importance (-ance).
